coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: No search spent (budget). Brunei is piped-water served; low likelihood.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Two searches; no Brunei lift/boiler certification rule or inspectors found (results were Malaysia/HK). Unverified; Labour Department or Ministry of Development is the likely home.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Brunei water supply is a government utility (Water Services Department); no small private water systems expected. Not searched.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: No Brunei pesticides order found; Poisons Act Cap 114 requires a licence from a Licensing Officer to import, possess for sale or sell poisons; Customs Application Permit for poisons and deleterious drugs per WTO notes; Agriculture Department controls restricted agri imports. coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies

Nothing new beyond K03/K04.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Societies Act Cap 66 (Registrar of Societies; registration order, Registrar may call for constitution and accounts, ss.11-14). No annual return duty confirmed. Halal supervision falls under K01.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: JPD and Royal Brunei Police enforce Road Traffic Act Cap 68; buses franchised and tendered; taxis franchised; e-hailing unregulated on price. No operator register or periodic report details found.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money-changers and remittance firms: BDCB licence under Money-Changing and Remittance Businesses Act Cap 174, annual fee BND 2,000 (money-changing) / BND 3,000 plus BND 55,000 guarantee (remittance), mandatory Compliance Officer since 1 May 2020, AML/CFT under Criminal Asset Recovery Order 2012, BDCB opens applications only periodically. Tamu/hawker licensing: nothing found.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: BDFA inspects food premises with scored checklist (70%+ satisfactory; below 51 unsatisfactory with counselling; 50 or less closed immediately) and requires Basic Food Safety Course for all food handlers. Draft Food Order 2024 would replace Public Health (Food) Act Cap 182 and regulate home-based businesses and stalls as food premises; gazettal not confirmed. Child care centres licensed by MCYS (KKBS) with multi-agency review (police record, traffic, fire, health, planning; 2019). Driving schools, tattoo studios, hunting: no data.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Retail petrol station licences issued by Ministry of Energy, Manpower and Industry (business.gov.bn). Petroleum Authority (PA) does quarterly compliance and safety inspections; 2008 directives require stations to file monthly sales records with Brunei Shell Marketing and use fleet cards; from 1 April 2026 stations must verify foreign plates under new fuel controls (asianews.network). Network is small and dominated by Brunei Shell Marketing. No LPG distributor licensing source found. Nothing strong.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: No commodity-trader regime found. Only rice, sugar, cooking oil, powdered milk and flour fall under the Price Control Act (Cap 142, amended 2021); traders of cooking oil and formula milk must apply to DEPS before selling. Rice is bought and supplied by the Treasury Department. See candidate on Price Control Act sellers.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Co-operative Societies Law (Cap 84, 1984 edition) with a Registrar; no annual-return portal, annual report or recent rule found. Source thin (icnl.org). Nothing found; sector small.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Only 54 registered private clinics in early 2025 (47 in 2024). Registration is administrative through the Private Healthcare Institutions Unit (set up June 2020, Boards Management Office, MoH). The Private Healthcare Institutions Order (PHIO) is drafted but not yet gazetted as of the 2025 Hansard answer. No insurer-billing or state-scheme reporting duty found. Watch item if the PHIO is gazetted.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Poisons Act licence (ss.5-6, 12-13) renewed through MoH Pharmaceutical Services Compliance and Licensing Section, application one month before expiry (Form B). Medicines Order 2007: import and wholesaler licences, mandatory product registration since July 2012. Misuse of Drugs Act enforced by Pharmacy Enforcement Section and the Narcotics Control Bureau. Customs permits for poisons. Few licensees and no controlled-drug register portal found. ODS (refrigerant) import permits go through BDNSW to JASTRE.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Security guard agencies are licensed by the Royal Brunei Police Force Security Guard Agency Licensed Division (AITI 2025 tender). The employment agency licence (Employment Agencies Order 2004, Labour Dept) is listed as no longer issued and temporary agencies are not recognised (business.gov.bn). Foreign Worker Licence (LPA) replaced the Labour Quota Licence: nothing new beyond K03. No cleaning-specific licence found.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Oil and gas local content is governed by Directive 2 (Local Business Development Framework, Energy Department PMO): operators, contractors and suppliers file LBD performance reports and Local Content Opportunity Framing reports; EIDPMO registration is compulsory for oil and gas companies with active contracts (business.gov.bn). Builder's licence (Building Control Order 2014) and contractor registration through ABCi / Ministry of Development. Sources are mostly 2012-2013 and the current process is unverified.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: AML Order and Terrorism Financing Order set CDD, suspicious transaction reports to the FIU (Attorney General's Chambers) and 5-year record keeping (arctic-intelligence.com, secondary source). Real estate permit issued by the Lands Department. Whether real estate agents and lawyers are designated DNFBPs, and the FIU reporting portal, were not confirmed. Arctic Intelligence already markets AML software for Brunei (see K12).

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Tourist accommodation premises, including short-term accommodation, must register with the Ministry of Primary Resources and Tourism under the Tourism Order 2016, since recodified (FAOLEX shows Tourism Act Cap 239, 2022 revision, Part V). A 2021 academic study found homestay licensing was slow and unclear. Guest-register format, levies and any platform duties were not confirmed. The sector is small.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Fish export permits (BND20 plus BND2 health certificate, 2016 fee schedule) and import/export permits run through the BDNSW national single window (see K08). MoH Food Safety and Quality Control Division issues food export certificates after premises inspection. Forestry sawmill licences and timber permits exist. Halal certification at Ministry of Religious Affairs: K01. Food ingredient import registration at MoH: K02. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 31. Fire Safety Order 2016: Fire Certificate and Fire Safety Certificate (Fire and Rescue Dept)
coverage.found: Fire Certificate is valid one year and must be renewed annually for commercial and industrial buildings (Hansard 14 Mar 2026, Minister of Development). The Fire Safety Regulations (Composition of Offences) 2020 apply. No online renewal portal or Brunei vendor found. See candidate.

coverage.category: 32. Workplace Safety and Health Order 2009: WSH Officers Regulations (amended 2025)
coverage.found: WSH (Workplace Safety and Health Officers) (Amendment) Regulations 2025, issued 9 Jan 2025 and effective 1 Jan 2025, widen the facilities that must appoint WSH officers; incident reporting regulations 2014 also apply. Thresholds were behind a paywall, so unverified.

coverage.category: 33. Price Control Act (Cap 142, amended 2021): controlled goods and sellers
coverage.found: Sellers of cooking oil and formula milk must apply to DEPS before selling; rice, sugar and flour are price controlled (flour seasonally at Ramadan/Syawal); 20 compounds in 9 months, BND500-1,000 for exceeding maximum price. Low value and small effort, mostly shop-floor compliance.

coverage.category: 34. Food premises: BDFA licences, grading programme, Food Handler Health Certificates (MoH FSQCD)
coverage.found: BDFA (est. 1 Jan 2021) issues certificates, licences and permits and runs a food-premises grading programme under the Brunei Darussalam Food Authority Order 2020, Public Health (Food) Act Cap 182 and Fresh Meat Order 2011 (amended 2020). The Food Handler Health Certificate is issued by MoH FSQCD; food premises also need halal certificate (3-year validity). Renewal intervals and fees were not found. Related to K01 and K02.

coverage.category: 35. BDCB-licensed money changers, remittance firms, pawnbrokers, money lenders
coverage.found: Money-changer licence (Cap 174) and Pawnbrokers Order 2002 licence from BDCB; new money-changer applications open only when announced. Very few licensees; no BDCB reporting portal details found. Not searched further (group A overlap).

coverage.found: Registration of Educational Institution certificate needs a letter of intent, premises assessment and ROCBN or Registrar of Societies registration (business.gov.bn). No periodic reporting rule found. Not searched further.
